items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The other changes were Brock in the place of Jack Butler and Benford in the place of Ted Fields.

ctx.x: We opened the Coliseum in October with a French orchestra on another stand and there were about 30 dancing hostess's engaged for men who came alone which was run on the taxi dance plan, but we did not play like the New York dancing school bands had to play. Willie also raised my salary to one thousand francs a week which was quite a good salary in 1938. The band now had two tenors and two altos. Big Boy Goldie was not with the band and Fletcher Allen had been hired in his place.

Fletcher had worked with Freddie Taylor and left to go to India with the first group that Leon had taken to Bombay. Joe Hayman was still there. The other changes were Brock in the place of Jack Butler and Benford in the place of Ted Fields.

Jimmy Monroe, who was the brother of Clark Monroe who had a famous club in Harlem, was in France because his wife Nina Mae McKinney who had starred in the first all-Negro movie produced in Hollywood "Halleluiah" was working in London, but Jimmy could not get permission to stay there and could only visit there for a few days at a time.
